cohort: Women who delivered between July and September (quarter 1) compared to those delivering between April and June (quarter 4) from 2017 to 2020.
finding: The July effect, marked by the beginning of residency for interns and increased responsibility for residents, has a minimal impact on obstetric complications overall, although postpartum length of stay and wound infection rates differed slightly between the two periods.
mod_finding: This study found no significant difference in cesarean delivery rates between the July-September period (when new residents begin) and the April-June period.
